observation_summary: The compiler enters an infinite recursion (StackOverflowError) when processing recursive inheritance or interface implementation chains, specifically when a type implements itself or forms a cycle.
hypothesis: The type resolution logic fails to detect cycles in the inheritance/implements graph because it only checks for implicit prototype cycles rather than the full inheritance cycle, leading to infinite recursion during subtype checks.
prediction: The fix will involve changing the cycle detection mechanism from checking only implicit prototypes to checking the entire inheritance chain, ensuring that recursive definitions are caught and handled before they cause infinite recursion.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows that the code was changed from calling 'detectImplicitPrototypeCycle()' to 'detectInheritanceCycle()'. This confirms that the original algorithm was insufficient for detecting the full scope of inheritance cycles, which is a procedural logic error in the type resolution algorithm.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a failure in the type resolution algorithm to correctly identify cycles in the inheritance graph. The fix replaces a narrow check (implicit prototype cycle) with a broader, correct check (inheritance cycle). This is a classic algorithmic correction where the procedure for validating the inheritance graph was incomplete, causing infinite recursion. It is not a missing guard (Checking) because the logic was present but insufficient, nor is it a design capability (Function/Class/Object) as the system already had cycle detection logic that just needed to be applied correctly.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves a check, the root cause is the logic of the cycle detection algorithm itself being too narrow, not a missing validation of input data.
The capability to detect cycles existed; the algorithm used to perform that detection was simply incorrect for the specific case of inheritance loops.
